target_customer: Startups that need to send payouts to workers, sellers or users in many countries
problem: Sending compliant payouts across countries and payment rails is slow and hard for a young company to build itself.
business_model: Usage-based payments API with fees per payout

founders.name: Gavin Mai
founders.background_notes: Only founder named on the YC page; no background given there.

exit.reason: Cause not public. YC lists the company as Inactive.

technical_complexity.rationale: Payments orchestration across countries needs banking partners, compliance and reliability, though built on existing rails.

defensibility.rationale: Sat on top of banking partners with established rivals offering payouts; no stated data or network advantage.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established payout providers kept the market; no acquisition of Carbon-12 found.

market_need_then: Not documented in found sources; the company positioned itself around startups struggling with global payouts.

branding.domain_note: Used carbon.money, a one word brand domain on a .money TLD.

brand_strength.rationale: A branding search found no press on the brand; the name collides with carbon credit firms and an unrelated faith based token called Carbon12.

outcome_analysis: Carbon-12 Labs joined YC in Winter 2020 with a global payouts API for startups and a solo founder named on the YC page. YC lists it Inactive, and no press, shutdown notice or founder post was found, so the cause is not public and failure factors are left empty.
notes: Company site carbon.money returned 403 so the site state is unknown. Both rounds rest on CB Insights alone (it lists 2.5M total over two rounds, a 0.5M convertible note in Jan 2020 and a 2018 seed with no amount; investors named in aggregate: Y Combinator, General Catalyst, Plug and Play Ventures, Digital Currency Group). The aggregator has placeholder values so these are weak. CB Insights gives 2017 founding and a New York address, conflicting with the empty directory location. Competitor list left empty: the dated search returned only current vendor pages, none from 2020. Rating for market need is unsupported by a source.
